summary.headline: Regaal FY26 operating income rose 23.9% to INR 1,134.2 crore and PAT reached INR 55.6 crore; 1,650 TPD expansion commissioned 26 May 2026, with no formal guidance until H1 FY27.
summary.overview: FY26 showed strong growth, with operating income up 23.9% YoY to INR 1,134.2 crore, value-added revenue up 18% to INR 295.8 crore, and PAT of INR 55.6 crore (4.9% margin). Q4 FY26 operating income was INR 244.6 crore, operating EBITDA INR 32.5 crore (13.3% margin) and PAT INR 16.5 crore. Crushing capacity was raised to 1,650 TPD on 26 May 2026 with liquid glucose, maltodextrin and a 10 MW power addition, and the capex estimate rose from about INR 430 crore to INR 540 crore. Management declined to give FY27 volume, margin or revenue guidance, promising a firm outlook by end of Q1/H1 FY27.

financial_highlights.change: Operating EBITDA margin 10.7% in Q3 per management

financial_highlights.value: INR 0.25 per share, subject to shareholder approval

segments.name: Native and modified starch, edible starch
segments.commentary: Native maize starch, edible starch, white/yellow dextrin and oxidised starch form the core; management said native starch was about 65% of the 825 TPD output in FY26, with co-products about 30% and value-added about 2-3%.

segments.name: Value-added / derivatives (new capacity)
segments.commentary: Liquid glucose at 180 TPD and maltodextrin powder at 50 TPD were commissioned 26 May 2026; 230 tons of DMH/DAH already commissioned. Management targets value-added at about 20-25% of revenue in FY27 and about 35% at full capacity.

segments.name: Consumer products and co-products
segments.commentary: Maize flour, custard powder, baking powder, icing sugar, germ, gluten, fibre and steep liquor are produced; management said co-product prices rose from March 2026 and starch prices recovered on reopened export markets.

segments.name: Trading of maize
segments.commentary: Trading contributed around 30%+ of revenue in the prior year per an analyst; management said it will fall to near zero as the new capacity absorbs the raw material.

guidance_outlook: No formal FY27 earnings guidance; management will provide a firm outlook between Q1 and H1 FY27 after the plant stabilises.
Ramp-up to full 1,650 TPD expected within about 15-20 days ('weeks, not months'), subject to no issues; management expects to reach 100% of rated capacity fairly quickly.
Management said revenue should at least double at full capacity, with cycles tied to maize prices; maize prices expected to be about 10% lower than last year, roughly INR 2 per kg.
Value-added share of revenue expected at about 20-25% in FY27 and about 35% at peak capacity; value-added margin delta guided at about 20-25% over starch prices.
Cash conversion cycle expected to move between 50 and 75 days, rising in Q1-Q2 with working capital peaking mid-year.
Total debt expected at about INR 700-750 crore during FY27 including working capital, against net debt of about INR 545.65 crore now.
Remaining capex of about INR 140 crore for FY27 after INR 401 crore spent by 31 March 2026 on a total of about INR 540 crore.
White-labelling volumes, currently 2-2.5% of starch volume with 4 partner companies, expected to rise considerably within H1 FY27.
capex_capacity: Crushing capacity expanded to 1,650 TPD, commissioned 26 May 2026, from 825 TPD in FY26; the largest maize milling facility in Eastern India per management.
Captive co-generation capacity raised by 10 MW to 15.8 MW total; 5 MW of the new 10 MW is being drawn at present. Approx. 81% of FY26 power needs were met captively.

Capex revised upward from about INR 430 crore to about INR 540 crore; INR 401 crore spent by 31 March 2026 and INR 140 crore to be spent in FY27. Commissioning of all facilities is expected over FY27.

Dextrose anhydrous (DAH) and dextrose monohydrate (DMH) to launch in Q3 to Q4 FY27 (around December-January); modified starch additions include cationic, carboxymethyl and pre-gel starch, gulal, spray starch and hydrol.
Storage: 65,000 MT of maize silos and godowns, plus about 240,000 MT of contracted warehouse capacity; procurement via 27 FPCs across six to seven districts; the 55-acre site has room for expansion.
demand_pricing: Maize prices are down versus last year (last year about INR 18-23/kg); management expects FY27 procurement prices about 10% lower, around INR 2/kg less, with farmer deliveries only starting from mid-May 2026 due to rain.
Starch prices recovered as export markets reopened; co-product (germ, gluten, fibre) prices rose sharply from March 2026 into Q1 FY27.
Management cited improved global cost competitiveness after the softening of raw material prices and a sizeable export order secured; South-East Asia is the focus market.
Customer base is 345 as of March 2026, with 134 added in FY26; dealer channel is 65.5% of annual revenue.
Management declined to disclose the revenue split across food, pharma and agriculture end-markets.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating margin fall QoQ from 19% to 14% per an analyst, when peers improved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management disputed the figures, saying operating EBITDA margin rose from 10.7% in Q3 to 13.3% in Q4; EBITDA fell in absolute terms due to costs ramped up ahead of the expansion, with steady-state margins expected from Q2 or Q3 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Bihar interest subvention and how is it accounted?
qa_highlights.answer: Subvention covers loan interest up to 10% per annum, capped at INR 20 crore over five years; receipts have typically come within about a quarter of application. It is booked as a receivable and credited against interest cost, so the 5% effective interest rate already reflects it.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital pattern and cash conversion cycle outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital rises in Q1, peaks around Q2 and falls from Q3 to Q4; the cash conversion cycle is expected to range between 50 and 75 days.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other current assets rise from INR 56 crore to INR 170 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Advances to maize suppliers and warehouses were given in March ahead of the 1,650 TPD ramp-up; advances rose from INR 45 crore to about INR 150 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How much value-added revenue is expected and at what uplift?
qa_highlights.answer: Value-added share is expected to rise from about 2-3% in FY26 to about 20-25% in FY27 and about 35% at full capacity; the delta over starch prices is about 20-25%, with a detailed margin guide promised in H1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue will the 1,650 TPD plant generate, and when will it run at optimum?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said revenue will at least double, with fluctuations tied to maize prices; the plant should ramp within about 15-20 days, but no firm date or utilisation guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is maize trading going to continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Trading will drop to near zero because the new capacity absorbs the raw material; any residual buying is to capture size discounts on MOQs, not for revenue.

risks_watch: Ramp-up of the 1,650 TPD plant and the DAH/DMH launch timing (Q3-Q4 FY27) are not yet proven; management has refused guidance until Q1/H1 FY27.
Debt is rising from about INR 546 crore net to roughly INR 700-750 crore total, and the working capital cycle is expected to swing between 50 and 75 days.
Revenue depends on maize price cycles; a sharp fall in maize prices could reduce turnover, and co-product and starch prices remain volatile.
The Bihar interest subvention is capped at INR 20 crore over five years and its timing depends on government processing; a delay would lift the effective cost of debt.
Sharp decline in FY26 Q4 EBITDA in absolute terms and a Q3 to Q4 margin dispute suggest the pre-commissioning cost base is still high.
Peak utilisation, value-added share and the detailed value-added margin guidance are expected by H1 FY27; the 20-25% starch-price premium is an unverified management estimate.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth and capacity, but notably cautious on near-term numbers: management repeatedly declined to give FY27 guidance, volume, margin or revenue figures, deferring them to Q1/H1 FY27. It was evasive on the value-added capex split and end-market revenue, and somewhat defensive when questioned about the QoQ margin decline.
